title: KV-cache & Batching Metrics Catalog + Dashboard Sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note to collect a compact, deployable set of telemetry signals and a lightweight dashboard layout focused on two cost/latency levers in the inference runtime: KV (prefix) cache effectiveness and request batching behavior. Goal is to have a minimal, high-utility view SREs and runtime engineers can use during incident triage and performance tuning.

Background / motivation:
- We get wide variance in tail latency and per-token cost that often maps back to cache misses and suboptimal batch packing. Current dashboards show end-to-end latency and qps but not the joint distribution of batch size, cache hit locality, and model variant fallbacks.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: prefer simple math and low-cardinality labels that are cheap to emit and easy to aggregate.

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: production-hosted and dedicated inference runtime only. Includes the edge cases where private deployments wire the same telemetry API.
- Non-goal: exhaustive token-level tracing for every request (that’s a separate tracing playbook). Here we propose a small set of spans/fields to connect traces to metrics.

Metric candidates (definitions are intentionally implementation-friendly):
1) kv_cache_request_count
   - what: number of requests that qualified for prefix/KV lookup
   - how: increment per incoming request (request-level), label with model, region, model_variant, route
   - owner: runtime/cache team

2) kv_cache_hit_rate (request-level)
   - what: fraction of requests with at least one useful cache hit used in generation
   - how: numerator = requests where cache_used == true, denominator = kv_cache_request_count in window
   - cardinality labels: model, region, model_variant, cache_tier (L1/L2), route
   - note: avoid per-token hit rate for low-cardinality; per-request boolean is cheaper and often sufficient

3) kv_cache_average_hits_per_request
   - what: average number of prefix hits or KV entries reused per request (can be zero)
   - how: emit an integer per request and aggregate with avg() over window
   - why: distinguishes many small hits vs a single long prefix reuse (impacts latency differently)

4) batch_size_distribution
   - what: sample distribution of batch sizes (1,2,3-4,5-8,9+ buckets)
   - how: emit batch_size bucket at batch-commit time; histogram preferred but buckets are fine
   - labels: route, model, region, autoscaler_pool

5) token_throughput_per_gpu
   - what: tokens/sec observed by a GPU/shard; helpful for capacity planning and identifying noisy tenants
   - how: local metric at host level aggregated to cluster/partition

6) model_variant_fallback_rate
   - what: percent of requests that fell back to a lower-cost or lower-capacity variant due to capacity or error
   - how: mark requests that were routed to fallback variant and count relative to total calls

7) effective_p99_generated_latency_excluding_queue
   - what: p99 of generation time (compute) excluding scheduling queue time; useful to separate queue pressure vs kernel perf
   - how: record timestamps at batch commit and generation end; subtract queue_wait_ms

8) queue_wait_time_percentiles
   - what: p50/p90/p99 of time spent waiting in scheduler before being included in a batch
   - why: often the main driver of perceived latency under load

Tracing guidance (lightweight, correlated with metrics):
- Basic spans to emit per request:
  * req.inbound (trace_id) - incoming HTTP request / API layer (include request_id, route, api_key_tier)
  * req.routing - routing decision and match (include model, preferred_variant, chosen_variant, fallback_reason if any)
  * req.cache_lookup - duration of KV/prefix cache lookup (emit cache_used boolean, hits_count integer)
  * batch.commit - batch creation event (emit batch_id, batch_size, queue_wait_ms)
  * gen.compute - generation kernel time on GPU (emit gpu_id, model_variant, tokens_generated)
  * req.outbound - response sent (status_code, bytes_sent)
- Sampling:
  * default: 1% tracing rate at LB for production; increase to 10% for high-error routes or emergency triage via sampling rules.
  * keep 100% of traces that have fallback_reason != "none" or status_code >= 500 to capture failure modes.
- Payloads / attributes: keep attributes low-cardinality. Use labels below: model, model_variant, route, pool, region, cache_tier. Avoid user IDs in traces.

Dashboard sketch (single-pane incident view + exploration tabs):
Top row (incident triage):
- Small sparkline: kv_cache_hit_rate (1m/5m) by model (top 3 models by call volume)
- Gauge: current avg batch size and % of single-request batches
- Alert banner: model_variant_fallback_rate (1m) > 0.5% (configurable)

Middle row (latency decomposition):
- Latency waterfall stacked area (p50/p90/p99): queue_wait | cache_lookup | gen.compute | serialization
- Heatmap: queue_wait_time_percentiles by pool and time-of-day (identify congestion patterns)

Bottom row (cost & throughput):
- tokens/sec per GPU (timeseries) with vertical lines for deploys/scale events
- bar: average kv_cache_average_hits_per_request by route (highly useful to see which endpoints benefit most)

Drilldowns / ad-hoc exploration:
- Trace search that pre-fills filters: model, variant, route, s.lo=500ms, fallback=true
- Batch-size histogram with ability to overlay response latency deciles
- Correlate cache_hit_rate drop with rollout tags (deploy id) and autoscaler scaling events

Operational playbook snippets (quick response):
- If p99 latency rises but gen.compute is flat: check queue_wait_time and batch_size skew. If queue_wait spikes, consider fast autoscale policy or temporary route throttling.
- If cache_hit_rate drops: verify cache invalidation events (deploys), and fallback_rate. If concurrent with spike in fallback_rate, investigate model_variant rollout.
- If batch_size distribution skews to 1: inspect incoming traffic burstiness and the batching scheduler backpressure settings. Consider increasing max_wait_ms for small routes for a short window.

Instrumentation checklist for rollout (minimum viable signals):
- emit per-request: request_id, model, model_variant, route, cache_used (bool), hits_count (int), chosen_variant, fallback_reason (nullable)
- emit per-batch: batch_id, batch_size, queue_wait_ms, timestamp
- ensure host-level tokens/sec and gpu_id are present in aggregation pipeline

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Per-token cache hit rate vs per-request boolean: per-token gives finer signal but increases cardinality and storage. Proposal: keep per-request boolean + avg_hits metric.
- Sampling thresholds: raising trace sampling for error routes improves debugability but we must cap storage costs. Need a short-term budget and automated downsampling.
- Dashboard retention: 30d for high-res metrics, 90d for daily aggregates. Ops to confirm retention cost vs audit needs.

Next steps / owners:
- Arjun: prototype batch_size_distribution histogram in staging by 2025-02-20
- Maya: add cache_used boolean to request event schema and wire up kv_cache_hit_rate in metrics pipeline by 2025-02-28
- Lina (observability infra): sketch dashboard tiles and alert rules by 2025-03-05

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add small sample traces to the doc for onboarding SREs (TODO)
- Check compatibility with private deployments (KMS + PII rules) — avoid trace attributes that contain user data

References and context links:
- Related Linear: OBS-421 (kv cache metrics)
- Runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime#882 (batching scheduler changes)
- Existing dashboard: observability/latency-slices-and-heatmap-dashboard-notes (useful context but different focus)

End of note. This is intentionally compact; expand metric definitions into a telemetry schema once owners sign off.
